newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nikko Sec says conducted no illegal deals.
newsitem.headline: Nikko Sec says conducted no illegal deals.

text.p: Nikko Securities Co Ltd said on Wednesday that it could not comment on a report that it transferred some 1.1 billion yen over seven years to accounts linked with a corporate racketeer at the centre of a payoff scandal, but said it believed there was no wrongdoing.

"We cannot comment on individual transactions. But we are convinced that we made no illegal deals," said a spokesman for Nikko, one of Japan's "Big Four" brokerages, referring to a report by the daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun on Wednesday.

The newspaper quoted an opposition lawmaker as telling a parliamentary committee on Tuesday that Nikko had transferred the biggest sum among 17 Japanese brokerages which had transferred a total of 1.7 billion yen over the seven-year period to March 1996 to accounts held at Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank Ltd (DKB) by the brother of racketeer Ryuichi Koike and his firm.
Nomura, meanwhile, had transferred a total of 8.5 million yen, the newspaper said.
The report spurred active sales of Nikko shares on the Tokyo bourse on Wednesday, sending the shares down 29 yen to 672 yen with turnover of 852,000 as of 0233 GMT.
The newspaper report made no suggestion that the fund transfers were illegal.
Tokyo prosecutors have so far arrested 10 DKB officials, including vice president Ichiro Fujita, on suspicion of making illegal loans to the "sokaiya" racketeer.
Sokaiya extort money from corporations by threatening to disrupt their shareholder meetings. Payoffs to sokaiya are banned by Japan's Commerical Code.
The scandal also involves Nomura Securities Co Ltd, where five people including a former president have been arrested.
